record.context_brief: First moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions
record.original_question: Let chi_{8d} denote the quadratic character attached to the fundamental discriminant 8d, with d ranging over odd squarefree integers 0 < d < X. Young proved a first-moment asymptotic of the form sum L(1/2, chi_{8d}) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2 + epsilon)). Improve this by reducing the exponent 1/2, ideally toward a secondary term of size c X^(1/4) plus a smaller error.

evidence.quote: Matthew Young [71] proved that sum_{0<d<X} L(1/2, χ8d) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2 + epsilon)). Alexandra Florea has suggested that sum_{0<d<X} L(1/2, χ8d) = X P(log X) + c X^(1/4) + O(X^ϑ) may be true for some c in R and ϑ in (0, 1/4). The goal would be to improve (18) by reducing the exponent 1/2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each odd squarefree positive integer $d$, let $\chi_{8d}$ denote the real primitive Dirichlet character modulo $8d$ associated with the fundamental discriminant $8d$ (the Kronecker symbol $\left(\frac{8d}{\cdot}\right)$), and let $L(s,\chi_{8d})$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function. It is known that there exists a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{R}[T]$ (of degree one) such that, as $X\to\infty$,
$$\sum_{\substack{0<d<X\\ d\text{ odd squarefree}}} L\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2},\chi_{8d}\right) \;=\; X\,P(\log X)\;+\;O\!\left(X^{1/2+\varepsilon}\right)$$
for every $\varepsilon>0$.

Improve this asymptotic by lowering the exponent $1/2$ in the error term. Specifically, prove an asymptotic of the form
$$\sum_{\substack{0<d<X\\ d\text{ odd squarefree}}} L\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2},\chi_{8d}\right) \;=\; X\,P(\log X)\;+\;c\,X^{1/4}\;+\;O\!\left(X^{\vartheta}\right)$$
for some explicit constant $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and some exponent $\vartheta\in(0,1/4)$, or otherwise reduce the exponent $1/2$ in the error term, identifying any secondary main terms that arise.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint by M. Čech ("First moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with secondary terms", arXiv:2509.03197) establishes an asymptotic of the form $X P_1(\log X) + X^{1/3} P_2(\log X) + O(X^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for a smoothed first moment of $L(1/2,\chi_{8d})$, with the error of size $X^{1/4+\varepsilon}$ conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis and the generalized Lindelöf Hypothesis. The secondary term is of order $X^{1/3}\log X$ (arising from the squarefree condition), rather than the conjectural $cX^{1/4}$ shape. Thus the problem of reducing the exponent $1/2$ has been addressed (conditionally), but the precise unconditional result and the exact $cX^{1/4}$ secondary term remain not fully established.

status_evidence.title: First moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with secondary terms
status_evidence.snippet: We obtain an asymptotic formula at the central point with error O(X^{1/4+epsilon}) ... main term X P_1(log X) + X^{1/3} P_2(log X)
status_evidence.claim: Čech (2025) establishes a refined first moment with secondary term of order X^{1/3} log X and error O(X^{1/4+epsilon}) conditional on RH and GLH, partially answering the call to reduce the exponent 1/2.

status_evidence.title: First moment of central values of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions
status_evidence.snippet: Refined first-moment asymptotics for L(1/2, chi_{8d}).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to refine first-moment asymptotics, indicating the problem is actively studied and not fully closed unconditionally.
